text:
aj: quick flag — onboarding IonBeam-v1. ran quant evals (8-bit/4-bit) and results look promising, but the bundled MODEL_LICENSE.txt has an odd clause. can legal take a look?
melissa-legal: paste the header or attach? we need the exact wording to assess redistrib/hosting impact.
aj: pasted below. the file lives at https://upstream.example/ionbeam/MODEL_LICENSE.txt but here's the relevant excerpt:

---
"Redistribution of model weights is permitted strictly for non-commercial research and educational purposes. Commercial use, hosting, or sublicensing of derived binaries or weights is prohibited without a separate commercial license. Attribution to IonLab is required in any public-facing product that uses the model.
"---

aj: our plan: run quant evals, and offer Optimized IonBeam quantized runtime in Redwood Dedicated for customers on reserved capacity. that would be hosting the model for paying customers.
devon: perf-wise 8-bit gives ~2.3x throughput improvement, 4-bit still buggy but promising. storing quantized weights in our dedicated bucket and loading into GPUless infra for private customers.
ellie-legal: immediate read: that excerpt looks like an NC requirement + attribution. "hosting" clause likely prevents commercial hosting for paying customers. distributing quantized weights in a package would be redistribution — also restricted. we need written upstream permission for commercial hosting or a commercial licensing addendum.
sanjay: could we avoid redistribution by keeping weights internal and only exposing inference? that still feels like "hosting" per the clause.
melissa-legal: correct — hosting inference for paying customers = commercial hosting. even if weights never leave our infra, offering access to paying customers violates NC unless we have license.
aj: what's our temporary allowed path to continue evals without breaching license?
ellie-legal: you can run internal evals (research use) and report results. do not package or ship quantized weights, do not provide model-as-a-service to paying customers. also ensure any eval artifacts we share externally have no weights baked in (e.g., logs, prompts, hashes ok).
devon: noted. we'll re-run evals in a gated sandbox. can we still commit quantization kernels to OSS repo if we reference architecture only?
melissa-legal: publishing kernels or optimization code that is independent of the weights is generally fine, but avoid including model-specific weight transforms that would enable redistribution. scrub repo for any sample weights or download scripts.
aj: action items: (1) ask IonLab for commercial license / clarify definition of "commercial" and whether Redwood Dedicated with customer-paid capacity counts, (2) re-run quant evals in private eval cluster, no packaging, (3) remove any weight download links from public repos, (4) draft attribution requirements to show customers if/when we get license.
ellie-legal: for the ask to IonLab include: intended use (hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private deployments), whether we plan to redistribute quantized weights, and whether IonLab can offer a commercial redistribution or hosting grant. cc their legal contact and include a proposed commercial attachment.
sanjay: can we craft a minimal attribution banner until license is sorted? example: "Model: IonBeam-v1 (IonLab). Used under license from IonLab. See https://ionlab.example/license for details."
melissa-legal: that wording is reasonable as a starting point but avoid asserting we have a license. prefer: "Model: IonBeam-v1 by IonLab. Usage subject to IonLab license." legal can refine.
aj: I'll open a ticket to contact IonLab and attach the eval logs.
eval-bot: eval-bot: job 9834 started (ionbeam-v1 quant sweep, internal only) :rocket:
devon: quick packaging snippet we will use for internal runs, explicitly excludes weights — sharing so legal can verify:

```
FROM ubuntu:22.04
COPY model-config.json /app/
COPY run_eval.sh /app/
# DO NOT COPY weights/
CMD ["/app/run_eval.sh"]
```

melissa-legal: good. please also add a check in CI that prevents accidental inclusion of a weights/ or checkpoints/ directory in any public release. we can add a pre-commit hook.
sanjay: noted. will add git hook and a build-time assertion.
ellie-legal: one more: check for export controls in IonLab jurisdiction. if IonLab is in region with export restrictions, there may be additional constraints on distribution or hosting across regions. please capture upstream country of origin.
aj: IonLab is listed as a UK entity on their repo. i'll ask them to confirm export/control status.
devon: timeline-wise, we can keep internal evals rolling this week. customer-facing offering blocked until license clarified.
aj: thanks all. I'll ping when I hear back from IonLab.
melissa-legal: thanks — if IonLab replies with a permissive commercial grant, require a copy of the signed doc before we ship; legal to review.
